admitted.text: Randi seems to treat her polished face as armour, and after the bench she seems to decide to keep the self Pace found hidden from him.
admitted.detail_quote: The one he had found was going back behind it, and she was not coming out again.

admitted.text: Being seen with tenderness seems to hurt Randi more than the spanking did.
admitted.detail_quote: the kind of flinch a body makes when something lands somewhere it was not braced for.

admitted.text: The bottle-cap moment hints that Randi turns overwhelming feeling into private pain she can control.
admitted.detail_quote: She kept the bottle when she was done, turning the cap loose in her fingers, and set the sharp inner edge of the cap under her thumbnail and pressed

admitted.text: Randi's appetite seems policed as tightly as her mother's, so food reads as a constant pressure in her.
admitted.detail_quote: an order that sounded like a sentence handed down, a drink the color of a bruise when it came

admitted.text: Randi's desire for Vee reads as real and helpless, arriving before she can dress it up as a gift for Pace.
admitted.detail_quote: Yes, she said. The word came out alone, with nothing around it

admitted.text: Randi seems able to want Vee only through Pace, picturing Vee's body as something she offers to him.
admitted.detail_quote: She had made herself not a woman who hungered for another woman, which he could see was unsurvivable, but a girlfriend offering her man a gift

admitted.text: When Pace gives Vee his attention, Randi reads as jealous or shut out, and her tension shows in her hands.
admitted.detail_quote: Beside her, Randi's hand went to her coffee cup, held it with both hands a second longer than the sip required

admitted.text: Randi reads as quietly arranging the coffee-shop "chance" meeting, apparently texting Pace to come.
admitted.detail_quote: the geometry arranged across thirty feet arrived all at once

admitted.text: Randi seems to spend her social standing on Vee in front of the sorority, which reads as both generous and claiming.
admitted.detail_quote: Randi had just spent something on her, in front of the girls who decided what it was worth.

admitted.text: Pace reads as patient and careful about consent, always giving the woman room to decide.
admitted.detail_quote: He wasn't going to take it any further than she had. Whatever came next was hers too.

admitted.text: Pace seems to enjoy handing Randi the power to choose, which also reads as a quiet way of steering her.
admitted.detail_quote: Greed now would spend the night early, and there was better ahead of her

admitted.text: For all his attentiveness, Pace seems blind to how badly the bench night shook Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: He thought that this had been a remarkably good evening.

admitted.text: Pace reads as calculating, able to predict Randi's moves before she makes them.
admitted.detail_quote: he had known since about the second block of the walk home

admitted.text: Pace seems to be growing loyal to Vee herself, keeping what she confided even from Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: He thought of what she had said after, on the walk — the true thing she had asked him to pretend she hadn't — and did not hand it over.

admitted.text: Pace seems to correct Vee without shaming her.
admitted.detail_quote: He had sliced it thin because she would eat thin slices and would not eat thick ones

admitted.text: Pace reads as self-denying, putting his own needs aside until his body pays for it.
admitted.detail_quote: She had shown him only a fraction of who she was, and tonight she had met more of herself than he had thought she would.

admitted.text: Pace's restraint in the truck reads as worshipful rather than grasping.
admitted.detail_quote: He sat and looked at all of her and didn't move

admitted.text: Pace seems shaped by an old guilt over going into a lover's private feelings uninvited.
admitted.detail_quote: Daphne had built a door, once, and he had not respected it.

admitted.text: Vee reads as starved to be chosen, and she is easily lit up by attention.
admitted.detail_quote: that she had been chosen, plainly, for reasons she didn't need to understand

admitted.text: Vee seems to have taken her mother's judgments into her own voice.
admitted.detail_quote: The voice said floozie in her mother's exact word and her thighs pressed once, hard, on their own

admitted.text: Vee's desire for Randi reads as strong and unadmitted.
admitted.detail_quote: all Vee could do was look at her with a flat helpless want

admitted.text: Vee seems ashamed of her own body and hides it under fabric.
admitted.detail_quote: She had worn the cardigan over the better shirt on purpose this morning, as she did most mornings

admitted.text: Vee seems to find her own agency with Pace and to insist that her choices were hers.
admitted.detail_quote: I wasn't talked into it. I did it because I wanted to and I did it on purpose.

admitted.text: Vee's shame seems to have become her arousal, so her mother's verdict feeds the heat.
admitted.detail_quote: that wanted to be the very thing the voice said, wanted it with him, wanted him watching her be it.

admitted.text: Vee seems to be drifting from Cassie toward Randi without wanting to look at it.
admitted.detail_quote: Underneath it something turned over, small, and she let it lie

admitted.text: Vee reads as dangerously ready to trust Pace because his patience feels like evidence that wherever he leads must be safe.
admitted.detail_quote: that she had been chosen, plainly, for reasons she didn't need to understand

admitted.text: Cassie reads as fiercely loyal, protecting Vee quietly.
admitted.detail_quote: Just her name, like setting something down where it wouldn't break.

admitted.text: Cassie reads as protective and wary of anyone who might take advantage of Vee.
admitted.detail_quote: She teased Vee about everything; she didn't tease her about this.

admitted.text: Cassie seems to sense something off about Randi before Vee does.
admitted.detail_quote: something passed over her face, brief, that Vee would not have been able to name

admitted.text: Cassie seems to see clearly that Pace looked past Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: He looked at you like he'd forgotten there was anyone else in the room

admitted.text: Brooke reads as a smiling watcher who files away information about Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: Pace. That's actually his name? Like he goes by Pace?

admitted.text: Brooke seems to hold quiet, total control of any room she sits in.
admitted.detail_quote: Brooke was the chapter president and did not need to stand to stop someone in her own common room.

admitted.text: Brooke's warmth toward Vee reads as appraisal, sizing her up behind the smile.
admitted.detail_quote: felt it take her measure, top to bottom, and stay warm the whole way.

admitted.text: Sloane reads as ambient social noise, the sorority chorus that grades without deciding
admitted.detail_quote: I love that you don't get pulled in by that stuff. It's so refreshing.

admitted.text: Kinsey reads as eager to fit in and a little off-key.
admitted.detail_quote: Kinsey, who had been waiting for the room to warm to her, leaned forward over her cereal bowl.

admitted.text: Christine seems motherly and generous toward Pace.
admitted.detail_quote: Christine fed me twice what I ordered and wouldn't put it on the bill.

admitted.text: Vee's mother reads as a constant voice of restraint over Vee's appetite.
admitted.detail_quote: *Floozies,* Vee thought, the word arriving whole and in her mother's voice before she had finished forming the picture.

admitted.text: The bench that hides inside a table: a hidden appetite in Pace's house, waiting to be uncovered again.
admitted.detail_quote: The top was leaning against the wall. The bench, which she had seen without seeing, was now bare.

admitted.text: The face in the mirror: a mask Randi wears over her real self.
admitted.detail_quote: She tried the smile again. The smile, this time, settled.

admitted.text: The lock and the key turning: Randi shutting herself away.
admitted.detail_quote: he heard the small click of the lock turning over, which was not a thing she had ever done before in his house.

admitted.text: The thin apple slices: rationed appetite and Pace's wish to feed Randi's hunger.
admitted.detail_quote: He had sliced it thin because she would eat thin slices and would not eat thick ones

admitted.text: Randi's blue toenails: her one hidden rebellion against her polish.
admitted.detail_quote: The one small place she let herself step out of line.

admitted.text: The Chi Latte sign: Vee finally let into a world she had stood outside.
admitted.detail_quote: She had stood outside this exact joke. Now she was walking under it

admitted.text: the crossed right-angle mark: separate difficult wants becoming legible when joined through Pace’s intervention
admitted.detail_quote: Put them together, at right angles, and they turn into a single thing that's suddenly plain

admitted.text: Being underwater: the place where Vee's body was never a problem, a lost innocence.
admitted.detail_quote: Nobody up there could see her. Nobody down here wanted anything.

admitted.text: The high window stools: being put on display for others to judge.
admitted.detail_quote: understood at once that she had been set up on a shelf.

admitted.text: The dry flannel: Pace's self-sacrifice and the shelter he gives Vee.
admitted.detail_quote: His only dry shirt. He opened his door and got out.

admitted.text: the burning maple: Randi’s desire arriving as an early, singular change she cannot yet contain
admitted.detail_quote: a single tree burning orange in a field of things that had not yet decided to change

admitted.text: the unnamed dishes: chosen surrender becoming nourishing because consent precedes Pace’s authority
admitted.detail_quote: She looked at what she'd agreed to without knowing, and it was better than anything she'd have known to ask for.

admitted.text: The cherry pits carried out on wax paper: an ethic of care and restraint taught without making the novice feel small.
admitted.detail_quote: She had it and he hadn't made her small to give it to her.

admitted.text: Will Vee be brought to the bench, and will she find out she was picked for it?
admitted.detail_quote: Do you think she'll like the bench?

admitted.text: What will happen when Vee learns that her apparently accidental friendships and romance began as Randi and Pace’s game?
admitted.detail_quote: Randi's *yes* had a name now and a class schedule

admitted.text: What will Randi do about the part of herself Pace uncovered?
admitted.detail_quote: The one he had found was going back behind it, and she was not coming out again.

admitted.text: What happened with Daphne, and what did it cost Pace?
admitted.detail_quote: he had gone in where he had not been asked, and it had cost him more than he had known

admitted.text: What did Cassie sense was ending when she said goodbye to Vee?
admitted.detail_quote: Something in the word caught, briefly, and her face did the thing it did with wrongness

admitted.text: Is what Randi holds back for Vee desire, jealousy, or both?
admitted.detail_quote: a want too big for her face, and keeping the face over it anyway.

admitted.text: Does Randi want Vee for herself, for Pace, or for an arrangement whose emotional terms she has not yet admitted?
admitted.detail_quote: Would you like to taste another woman?

admitted.text: Will Brooke and the sorority see what is going on between Randi and Vee?
admitted.detail_quote: Randi had just spent something on her, in front of the girls who decided what it was worth.

admitted.text: What was Vee about to tell Pace when the siren cut her off?
admitted.detail_quote: The thing she wanted to say was bigger than any words she had for it

admitted.text: When will Vee recognize that her helpless wanting includes Randi herself rather than only the life Randi opens to her?
admitted.detail_quote: and the want had nowhere to put itself except *here, this, with her,*
